Walmart owner reviews split between daily users who call the stitches neat and the body sturdy, and a minority reporting bobbin winding faults, pedal unresponsiveness, and machines that stopped after a week.

editorial.verdict: A computerized Singer Heavy Duty with LCD stitch selection and a metal-frame claim; owner reports on build and reliability are mixed.
editorial.whoFor: A beginner who wants push-button stitch selection, an LCD readout and six one-step buttonhole styles at the low end of the computerized Heavy Duty line.
editorial.skipIf: You want an automatic thread cutter, a walking foot in the box, or a published stitch count; Singer gives 215 applications and no count.

faqs.q: What do owners say about the Singer 6600C?
faqs.a: Owner reports are mixed and lean toward problems. Of 11 statements on build quality, 9 are negative, with some owners saying it is not the all-metal machine the name suggests, and 9 of 10 on defects are negative, including an error on day one, a needle that sticks down and a machine that stopped and started in bursts. A smaller group finds it quiet, easy to thread and stronger on thick fabric than their old machines. Reddit leans toward people asking for help, so problems are over-represented; Amazon shows 4.4 of 5 from 158 ratings (seen 2026-10-01).

faqs.q: What are the common problems with the Singer 6600C?
faqs.a: Defects (10 voices) and build quality (11 voices) are the two recurring themes, nearly all negative. Examples are an EL error on day one, a needle that sticks in the down position, tension that stopped holding after a needle change, and loud shaking at thick folded denim seams. Noise is split, with 4 of 6 voices calling the machine quiet. These are mostly help-seeking posts, not a failure rate.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Singer 6600C and the 6700C?
faqs.a: On Singer's pages the 6600C lists 215 stitch applications, 6 one-step buttonhole styles and 5 feet with no walking foot, while the 6700C lists 411 applications, 7 buttonhole styles, a lettering font, 10 feet including an even feed (walking) foot and a speed control lever. Both list a metal interior frame, 15.4 lb and a manual speed of 1000 +/- 50 stitches per minute, though the 6700C manual is shared with the 6705C. Seen prices were $319.99 for the 6600C on 2026-10-01 (extension-table bundle page) and $329.99 for the 6700C on 2026-09-29 (dealer sale price against a $419.99 list), so confirm what is in each box. Stitch counts are application counts, not built-in patterns [verify].

faqs.q: How many stitches does the Singer 6600C have?
faqs.a: Singer advertises 215 stitch applications and publishes no separate stitch count, so the built-in figure is [verify]. Dealers quote 100 and one comparison site 200. Applications count techniques, not patterns.

faqs.q: Does the Singer 6600C have an automatic thread cutter?
faqs.a: None is published. Singer's manual lists a manual thread knife for trimming ends, and one comparison site lists the automatic cutter as a 6800C feature.

faqs.q: Is the Singer 6600C good for beginners?
faqs.a: Singer sells it into that market: LCD stitch selection, a top drop-in bobbin and a built-in needle threader. Of 4 owner voices on threading, 3 are positive, but defects and build quality are the larger themes, so check the return terms.

faqs.q: Can the Singer 6600C sew denim and canvas?
faqs.a: Singer's copy says it is designed with heavy duty projects in mind, from denim to canvas, which is a claim; Heavy Duty is a series name, not a duty rating. Owners are split: 2 voices say it sews thicker fabric better than their other machines and 2 report seizing, a jammed needle or loud shaking at thick folded denim seams. Singer publishes a 6 mm presser foot lift and no motor wattage, and lists no walking foot [verify].

faqs.q: What is the price of the Singer 6600C?
faqs.a: Singer's extension-table bundle page showed $319.99 on 2026-10-01, against a $448.98 strike-through list price that is a comparison figure, not a selling price. The standalone machine page redirects to Singer's homepage, so the machine is currently listed there as a bundle. Prices drift weekly, so use the price band on this page as the stable guide.
